research_question: How did surveyors establish Mount Everest's height, and why do modern measurements require a reference datum?

sources.title: Mount Everest height confirmed at 8,848.86 metres
sources.publisher: Government of Nepal, Department of Survey
sources.reliability: Official national surveying agency; source homepage used for the joint height announcement
notes: Nepal and China jointly announced 8,848.86 metres in December 2020.
The official figure is a defined elevation measurement, not height from the mountain base.

sources.title: Mount Everest: The First Survey
sources.reliability: Established UK learned society and geographical research institution
notes: Historic Himalayan surveying used triangulation and long-distance observations.
Peak XV was identified as exceptionally high through nineteenth-century surveying.

sources.title: Geodetic Surveying
notes: Geodetic networks and reference systems are required for consistent coordinates and heights.
Satellite coordinates need datum interpretation before they can be treated as sea-level elevation.

sources.title: Geodesy and the Earth's shape
notes: The Earth is not a perfect sphere; reference ellipsoids and geoid models underpin modern height systems.
Vertical reference systems allow measurements from different locations to be compared.

sources.title: Mount Everest
notes: Everest's elevation has been refined over time as surveying methods improved.
Mountain height is conventionally compared by elevation above sea level.
